evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.151: bēstiae volātilēs (Lewis & Short s.v. volātilis)
terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work has a word for a drone. māchinula is late (Paulinus of Nola) but the modern word for small appliances (see device); volātilis, flying, is Cicero’s. The English name comes from the bee’s hum; the bee’s Latin name, fūcus (see drone, the male bee), is not used of the machine here, since the metaphor is English.

phrases.latin: Ecce māchinula volātilis! Audīsne ut strīdeat?
phrases.english: Look, a drone! Can you hear it whirring?

sources: Lewis & Short: machinula · Lewis & Short: volatilis
